text:
jordan: Heads-up — noticed a gap in VPC flow logs for eu-west-1 starting ~02:10 UTC and simultaneous GPU pool provisioning failures. Some instances are throwing KMS errors. Looks like our autoscaler surged preemptibles and KMS started throttling.

maya: Ugh. Do you have the error lines?

jordan: Error from provisioning agent: `Failed to unwrap volume key: KMS ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded`
jordan: Also seeing `FlowLogStatus: INACTIVE` for several subnets when I ran a quick check.

ops-bot: [alert] gpu-autoscaler triggered surge: +220 preemptible workers in eu-west-1 at 02:12 UTC — cost-alert sent to billing.

devon: There was a security change last night — I merged a NACL tighten PR across eu-west to block ephemeral outbound to 10.5.0.0/16 due to noisy egress. Could that have hit the KMS endpoint or flow log delivery? PR: https://github.com/redwood-infra/infra/pull/1298

maya: KMS is a regional service with endpoints in the AZ; if we blocked egress to monitoring/logging endpoints or S3 delivery IPs that would break flow logs delivery and maybe KMS if internal endpoints are IP-based. Can you paste the `aws logs` check?

jordan: Ran: ```
# aws ec2 describe-flow-logs --filter Name=status,Values=ACTIVE,INACTIVE --region eu-west-1
{
  "FlowLogs": [
    {"FlowLogId":"fl-0a1b2c3d","ResourceType":"Subnet","ResourceId":"subnet-abc","LogDestinationType":"s3","State":"INACTIVE"},
    {"FlowLogId":"fl-0x9y8z7","ResourceType":"Subnet","ResourceId":"subnet-def","LogDestinationType":"cloud-watch-logs","State":"ACTIVE"}
  ]
}
```

jordan: And kube-provisioner logs: `kms: access denied` and `dial tcp <kms-ip>:443: i/o timeout` from a few nodes.

security-bot: [audit] last change to NACL euw-nacl-3 by devon at 2026-09-12T23:58:44Z — rule 102 (egress 0.0.0.0/0 deny) applied to 10.5.0.0/16 range.

devon: That deny was meant to target a bad tenant net; I didn't realize it overlapped the NAT instance egress range. My bad — rolling back rule 102 now.

ops-bot: command: `aws ec2 revoke-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id euw-nacl-3 --rule-number 102 --egress`

jordan: After rollback, I see KMS requests returning 200 from the agent logs. Flow log delivery still shows a few INACTIVE for ~2m.

kai: We should still open a quota request with KMS — surge created a large burst of encrypt/decrypt keys. If KMS was throttling, other customers might be affected. I'll file a support case and a short postmortem.

maya: +1. Also let's add an allow rule for the KMS IP ranges and S3/CloudWatch log endpoints in the NACL/security-group docs so this doesn't regress. Put it in infra runbook.

jordan: Created incident ticket INF-4521: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521 — title: "Euw VPC flow logs missed + KMS throttle during preemptible surge". Added timeline and logs.

sre-incident-bot: Incident INF-4521 triaged to Sev3. Oncall: kai.

kai: Action items: 1) Devon confirm NACL rule rollback completed and add exception rules for KMS/S3/CWL. 2) I will submit KMS quota/support + include request for burst handling guidance. 3) Jordan to run full scan for other regions for INACTIVE flow logs and reconcile with billing surge. 4) Maya to update runbook and open PR for explicit allow ranges and test harness.

devon: Rollback confirmed. Will follow up with PR in infra repo and tag security for review.

jordan: Scanned other regions — no other gaps. Just eu-west surge event.

maya: We should also add a Canary to the deployment pipeline that verifies flow logs active post network rule changes. I'll sketch it.

kai: Ok — closing on slack thread. Will post incident summary once KMS support responds. Thanks all :thumbsup:
